text:
Boston's four-game winning streak ended at TD Garden, and it ended early. Montreal scored twice in the first period and three times in the second, and the Canadiens led 5-0 before Casey Mittelstadt got the Bruins on the board late in the middle frame. Jacob Fowler, a goalie Montreal drafted 69th overall in 2023 and who arrived from Boston College, stopped 30 of 32 shots and was named the game's first star.

The scoreboard flatters Montreal's play a little. Our expected goals model, which grades every shot by how often it goes in, had the Canadiens at 3.29 and the Bruins at 2.88, and when we replay every shot, Montreal wins 57 percent of the time. At even strength Boston was actually the better team, 2.77 to 2.08, and it took 64 shot attempts to Montreal's 48. Montreal blocked 23 shots to Boston's six, and it got its chances early: 1.85 expected goals in the first period against 1.13. Phillip Danault's slap shot, a 3 percent chance, made it 5-0. Jeremy Swayman allowed four goals on 17 shots, about 1.8 more than the quality of those shots deserved, and Michael DiPietro finished the night in relief.

Mittelstadt, drafted eighth overall by Buffalo in 2017, scored twice, once late in the second and again 53 seconds into the third, both with Elias Lindholm assisting. The Bruins out-chanced Montreal in each of the last two periods, but the gap was already too wide. Boston goes home with its streak gone and a long night of work in goal to review. Montreal leaves with a win built on a quick start and a rookie goalie.
